Fingerprints.question: 1) Fingerprint is the pattern of:
Fingerprints.exp: Fingerprint is formed by the pattern of epidermal ridges on the finger pulp. These ridge patterns are used for personal identification.

Fingerprints.question: 2) The main forensic use of fingerprint is:
Fingerprints.exp: Fingerprint is an important method of personal identification. It is considered highly reliable because ridge patterns are unique.

Fingerprints.question: 3) Fingerprint is considered an absolute method of identification because:
Fingerprints.option1: It is affected by sex hormones
Fingerprints.option4: No two persons have identical fingerprints
Fingerprints.exp: Fingerprints are unique to each person. Even identical twins do not have identical fingerprint patterns.

Fingerprints.question: 4) Fingerprints were first used by:
Fingerprints.exp: Fingerprints were first used by William Herschel in Bengal, India.

Fingerprints.question: 5) Fingerprints were first used in:
Fingerprints.exp: William Herschel first used fingerprints in Bengal, India. This is an important historical point in forensic identification.

Fingerprints.question: 6) Fingerprints were first used in the year:
Fingerprints.exp: William Herschel first used fingerprints in Bengal, India, in 1858. This fact is important in forensic history.

Fingerprints.question: 7) Fingerprints develop during intrauterine life around:
Fingerprints.exp: Fingerprint patterns develop around 12–16 weeks of intrauterine life. Once formed, they remain unchanged throughout life.

Fingerprints.question: 8) Fingerprint pattern remains:
Fingerprints.exp: Fingerprints remain permanent throughout life. Only size may increase with growth, but the ridge pattern remains the same.

Fingerprints.question: 9) The most common fingerprint pattern is:
Fingerprints.exp: Loop is the most common fingerprint pattern. The file mentions its frequency as about 60–65%.

Fingerprints.question: 10) The approximate frequency of loop pattern is:
Fingerprints.exp: Loop is the commonest fingerprint pattern and accounts for about 60–65%. Whorl, arch and composite are other patterns.

Fingerprints.question: 11) Whorl belongs to which group?
Fingerprints.exp: Whorl is one of the fingerprint patterns. Other patterns include loop, arch and composite.

Fingerprints.question: 12) Arch is a type of:
Fingerprints.exp: Arch is a fingerprint pattern. It is less common than loop.

Fingerprints.question: 13) Composite pattern is related to:
Fingerprints.exp: Composite is included among fingerprint patterns. The main patterns are loop, whorl, arch and composite.

Fingerprints.question: 14) Fingerprint is permanently destroyed by injury involving:
Fingerprints.exp: Deep injury involving the dermis can permanently destroy fingerprints. Superficial epidermal injury does not permanently destroy the pattern.

Fingerprints.question: 15) Fingerprints after death can be used until:
Fingerprints.exp: Fingerprints may be used after death as long as skin is preserved. Once decomposition destroys the skin, fingerprint identification becomes difficult.
